item.text:
**Assessment**
Mixed, leaning no. In 2024 there were real stabilization and trade/investment-facilitation steps, but the broader rules environment still looked constrained by corruption, bureaucratic hurdles, weak property-rights enforcement, and politically distorted investment choices.

**Positive / Partial**
- **Bangladesh: Second Reviews Under the ECF/EFF and RSF Arrangements** | IMF | June 24, 2024 | https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/186/article-A001-en.xml | The IMF said program performance was broadly on track and highlighted exchange-rate realignment, a crawling peg, tighter monetary policy, and tax/subsidy reforms as steps to safeguard macro stability and improve conditions for investment. `Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.3`
- **Bangladesh Receives $900 Million World Bank Financing to Increase Economic and Urban Resilience for Sustainable Growth** | World Bank | June 21, 2024 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/21/bangladesh-receives-900-million-world-bank-financing-to-increase-economic-and-urban-resilience-for-sustainable-growth | The World Bank described reforms that would shift Bangladesh from trade taxes toward consumption and income taxes, institutionalize e-procurement, strengthen banking oversight, and support public and private investment. `Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.3`
- **World Bank Helps Bangladesh Develop Bay Terminal** | World Bank | June 28, 2024 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-develop-bay-terminal | The Bay Terminal project was framed as a way to cut import/export costs, improve port efficiency, and mobilize private investment through international terminal operators, which is a genuine pro-trade / pro-investment rule improvement. `Question IDs: 5B.4`
- **BIDA's first State of Investment Climate Webinar describes changes to encourage economic development and investor trust** | Bangladesh Investment Development Authority | October 30, 2024 | https://www.boi.gov.bd/details/bangladesh-investment-webinar-describes-changes-encourage-economic-development-and-investor-trust | Government officials promoted process changes such as a “project ambassador” and smoother investor engagement, which points to an effort to improve investment conditions, though this is more reform messaging than proof of durable results. `Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.2`

**Negative / Counterevidence**
- **Financial Sector and Fiscal Policy Reforms Will Help Bangladesh Sustain Strong Growth** | World Bank | April 2, 2024 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/02/financial-sector-and-fiscal-policy-reforms-will-help-bangladesh-sustain-strong-growth-despite-strong-growth-south-asia-r | The World Bank said growth was being disrupted by high inflation, a persistent balance-of-payments deficit, and financial-sector vulnerabilities; it also said investment was dampened by tight liquidity, rising interest rates, import restrictions, and higher input costs. `Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.3`
- **Bangladesh Development Update - Special Focus : Creating Jobs for a Better Future** | World Bank | October 1, 2024 | https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099104310142425439 | The report says most SMEs faced high regulatory costs, unreliable infrastructure, and limited access to finance, and that stronger competition policy, competitive neutrality for state-owned enterprises, and streamlined trade policies were still critical for private-sector-led growth and jobs. `Question IDs: 5B.4`
- **Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House said property rights were unevenly enforced and that corruption, bribery, bureaucratic and regulatory hurdles, and considerable state interference constrained private economic activity. `Question IDs: 5B.4`
- **Factbox-Troubled Bangladesh's economy bogged down by high unemployment, inflation** | Reuters | August 8, 2024 | https://m.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/factboxtroubled-bangladeshs-economy-bogged-down-by-high-unemployment-inflation-3561503?ampMode=1 | Reuters summarized widening external deficits, taka depreciation, falling reserves, an IMF bailout, and stagnant private-sector job creation, which undercuts the idea that 2024 preserved a healthy investment climate. `Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.3`
- **AL govt created lawless economy** | The Daily Star | October 31, 2024 | https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/al-govt-created-lawless-economy-3741796 | A white-paper lead said authoritarian practices produced crony capitalism and a nexus of bureaucrats, political leaders, and business interests that captured public organizations, which is direct evidence against fair, neutral economic rules. `Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.2`
- **Rooppur Power Plant was AL govt's white elephant: energy sector experts** | TBS News | October 5, 2024 | https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801 | Energy-sector experts described Rooppur as a mismanaged, corruption-linked white elephant, suggesting major investment decisions were still shaped by patronage rather than neutral economic merit. `Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.2`

**Search Gap**
I did not find a 2024 source showing Hasina personally creating a broad, durable pro-competition / pro-property-rights regime. The strongest positives are macro stabilization and some logistics/investment-facilitation reforms; the stronger governance evidence still points to a business environment constrained by state favoritism, weak enforcement, and politicized allocation.
